brief.headline: The 31-July official finally published and it answered the week's open question the wrong way for the bulls: the cash-3M backwardation collapsed from +$44.00 to +$17.00 in a single session while cash fell $35.00 to $3,196.00 - yet exchange stock drew AGAIN to a fresh century low of 264,400 t, so availability tightened on the very session the prompt premium halved.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: the first LME official struck after China's July manufacturing PMI came in at 49.2 took cash down $35.00 (-1.08%) to $3,196.00, but the 3-month only $8.00 (-0.25%) to $3,179.00. Almost the entire adjustment landed in the prompt, compressing the backwardation by $27.00 to +$17.00 - back to where it sat on 28-Jul, before the three-session widening run. The forward curve barely flinched; the nearby did all the work.

WHY IT MATTERS: a prompt premium that expands regardless of flat-price direction is usually read as physical scarcity. This one gave back 61% of its widening on the first demand shock it met, which points to a meaningful macro and positioning component in the late-July move rather than pure scarcity. The offsetting fact is stubborn: LME stock fell another 1,900 t to 264,400 t, a 23rd consecutive session of draws and a fresh low this century, -48.1% year-to-date. Availability and the spread disagreed on the same day, and only one of them can be right for long.

THE 48 HOURS: the weekend hardened the supply side rather than the demand side. Two more vessels were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday - a tanker struck by a projectile about 20 km north-east of Lima, Oman, with engine-room damage (UKMTO) - after only about ten commodity vessels transited on Friday against more than 100 before the war (Kpler via The National). Bab al Mandeb is also now impaired, running 31 vessels on Friday after a weekly low of 16 following the Houthi embargo on Saudi shipping. Against that, SMM reported outside-China daily-average output UP 1.6% month-on-month on Middle East and Iceland restarts, and said explicitly that the renewed conflict has not so far re-interrupted smelter production.

WHAT TO WATCH: Monday brings the first August LME official - whether +$17.00 stabilises, rebuilds or flips toward contango is now the single most informative number on the board - alongside China's Caixin manufacturing PMI as the private-sector cross-check on 49.2. Then whether stock breaks 260,000 t, whether Hormuz transit counts recover from single digits, and the alumina index, which SMM has testing the 2,600 yuan/t threshold as excess supply beats cost support.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: BACKWARDATION (cash ABOVE 3M) at +$17.00 on the 31-Jul official, down from +$44.00 on 30-Jul - a $27.00 compression in a single session, the largest one-day narrowing of the current move and a 61% give-back. Convention: cash > 3M = backwardation = nearby tightness; cash < 3M = contango. The structure is still backwardated, so the prompt is still bid - but the late-July widening sequence (+$16.00 on 28-Jul, +$30.00 on 29-Jul, +$44.00 on 30-Jul) has retraced almost entirely to its starting point on the first official struck after China's contractionary PMI. THE HONEST READ: the prior compile named holding above roughly +$40.00 as strong confirmation the tightness was physical, and a collapse toward flat as evidence the spread carried macro and speculative content. The outcome is between the two but closer to the second. The counter-evidence is that exchange stock drew a further 1,900 t to a century low on the same session - so availability did not loosen even as the prompt premium halved.

lme.commentary: SUNDAY COMPILE, FIRST BOARD OF AUGUST: every official here is the 31-JULY-2026 print, which published on Westmetall over the weekend and is the figure the previous compile could not yet see. No exchange session takes place on Saturday or Sunday, so nothing on this board will change before Monday's ring. THE SESSION ITSELF: cash settled $3,196.00, down $35.00 (-1.08%) from $3,231.00; the 3-month settled $3,179.00, down only $8.00 (-0.25%) from $3,187.00; stock fell 1,900 t to 264,400 t. THE HEADLINE IS THE SPREAD. Cash-3M compressed from +$44.00 to +$17.00 - a $27.00 single-session narrowing and a 61% give-back of the three-session widening run that ran +$16.00, +$30.00, +$44.00 through the final week of July. This was the print the prior compile named as the week's most informative number, on the explicit test of whether the backwardation held above roughly +$40.00 into the first official struck after China's 49.2 manufacturing PMI. It did not. The structure is still backwardated, so the prompt is still bid, but the conclusion has to be recorded honestly: a material part of the late-July widening was carrying macro and positioning content rather than pure physical scarcity. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE MATTERS EQUALLY. Exchange stock drew a further 1,900 t on the same session to 264,400 t - a 23rd consecutive published session without a build, a fresh low this century on LME records back to January 1998, and -48.1% year-to-date from 509,250 t on 02-Jan - with the available on-warrant component at a 16-month low. Availability tightened on the very day the prompt premium halved. Those two facts cannot both be the whole story, and Monday's first August official is the next print that arbitrates. WHERE THE MOVE LANDED: cash fell more than four times as far as the 3-month in percentage terms, so the entire adjustment was in the nearby rather than the curve. Trading Economics' independently published traded reference for the same session closed $3,194.65, flat at +0.02%, sitting between the two officials - corroboration that the forward barely moved. MONTH IN CONTEXT: July's published monthly means are now locked and inclusive of the 31-Jul print at cash $3,155.98 and 3M $3,148.93, 8.7% below June's $3,458.64, with average stock of 282,350 t against June's 320,314 t. July was the month the June war-spike deflated into a higher floor - and the month ended near, not at, its high, with the month's peak official cash of $3,231.00 set on 30-Jul and given back the next day.

PERIODIC ASSESSMENT, not a daily mark - no fresher free public print is available at this 02-Aug refresh, so the value is held at its assessment date rather than implied to have moved. The duty-unpaid leg is the cleanest read on genuine European physical tightness because it excludes both the 6% EU import duty and the CBAM cost embedded in duty-paid assessments since January 2026. The regional backdrop turned marginally tighter over the weekend: with Bab al Mandeb impaired alongside Hormuz, the Suez routing that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam is no longer a clean alternative corridor.

Billet premiums carry the duty-paid structure plus the conversion spread over P1020, so they move with both metal availability and extruder order books; European extrusion demand remains the soft spot in the regional balance, and TTF gas around EUR 59.07/MWh at the 31-Jul close (+1.29% on the session) still caps restart economics - though Hydro's Slovalco agreement with the Slovak government to resume 75,000 t from Q4-2026 is the first concrete European restart of the cycle. drivers.text: Both Gulf chokepoints are now impaired at once - Hormuz ran about ten commodity vessels on Friday against more than 100 pre-war, with two further attacks on Saturday, while Bab al Mandeb fell to a weekly low of 16 — Kpler data via The National (01-Aug-2026) puts Friday's Hormuz transits at roughly ten commodity vessels - seven exiting, three inbound, two of them with transponders switched off - after a week running 7, 11, 15, 4 and 10, against more than 100 daily before the war began on 28-February. UKMTO reported two further incidents on Saturday 01-Aug: a tanker struck by a projectile about 20 km north-east of Lima, Oman, with engine-room damage and no casualties, and a large splash and explosion near a second tanker 40 km north-east of Khasab. Separately Bab al Mandeb - the Red Sea gateway that had been the workable alternative - collapsed to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by Friday. US Central Command maintains the strait is open and reports rerouting 30 commercial vessels, disabling two and boarding two as at 31-Jul under the blockade reimposed on 14-Jul. Two impaired chokepoints rather than one is a structurally higher delivered-cost regime for any Gulf-origin or Suez-routed cargo.
drivers.source: The National - How many ships are transiting through Hormuz and Bab Al Mandeb? (01-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: Gulf war-risk cover at 3-10% of hull value - over $7 million per transit on a $100m vessel versus 0.25% pre-war - and Saturday's attacks make near-term softening improbable — AL Circle's 24-Jul Middle East review assembles the public picture: war-risk insurance for Gulf transits stood at roughly 0.25% of hull value before February's escalation, quadrupled within three weeks of the first strikes, and by mid-July was quoted at 3-10% - the difference between a $250,000 premium and one exceeding $7 million on a single transit. Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice. The five GCC smelters produced about 6.16 Mt in 2025 (roughly 8% of world supply) with more than 80% exported; analysts now pencil in 3-3.5 Mt of losses through 2026, near 5% of global primary supply. The 30-Jul LNG exit briefly suggested a two-way direction; Saturday's two attacks removed that, and insurance reprices on underwriters' cycles rather than transit counts, so the wedge persists even through quiet weeks.
drivers.source: AL Circle - 2026 Middle East aluminium outlook: 5% of global supply, USD 7 million insurance and the Hormuz effect (24-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: US Section 232 at 50% is $1,598.00/t of the US duty-paid premium at the 31-Jul cash - the rate was re-verified unchanged this run and the tariff leg fell $17.50 purely because the metal price fell — Aluminium articles made entirely or almost entirely of aluminium pay 50% ad valorem on full customs value; derivative aluminium content pays 25%. The structure originates in the April-2026 proclamation and was further adjusted by the 01-Jun-2026 proclamation (Federal Register 2026-11314, effective 08-Jun-2026), whose 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 window applies to the Annex I-C reduced-rate carve-outs - 15% all-in for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members. A 20-Jul-2026 proclamation additionally lets companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) import at half the applicable rate; no CBP guidance for that measure has been issued yet. MECHANICS: at the 31-Jul cash official of $3,196.00 the tariff leg is 0.50 x 3,196.00 = $1,598.00/t, down from $1,615.50 at the 30-Jul cash. The policy leg moves with the metal price whether or not the physical market changes at all - this run it fell for arithmetic reasons alone.
drivers.source: Federal Register 2026-11314 - Further adjusting the tariff regimes for imports of aluminum, steel and copper (June 2026); CBP Section 232 guidance

drivers.text: The domestic-supply answer to the US premium is arriving: Mt. Holly at full capacity since 27-Jul and a Marston, Missouri potline restart adding 75,000 t/y by end-2026 — Century's Mt. Holly returned to full capacity on 27-Jul for the first time since 2015 after a $50m potline restart, adding roughly 10% to total US primary output, credited publicly to Section 232. SMM's 31-Jul overseas production review adds that Magnitude 7 Metals will restart the No.1 potline at its Marston, Missouri smelter, adding 75,000 t/y of primary capacity by the end of 2026. Both are tariff-induced import substitution: each tonne produced domestically is a tonne that no longer needs to clear a 50% duty, which over time compresses the duty-paid premium the tariff created. The effect is slow - US primary capacity is small relative to consumption - but the direction is now established rather than announced, and Century's Q2 results on 06-Aug are the first P&L test of it.
drivers.source: SMM Analysis - overseas production update (31-Jul-2026); Century Aluminum disclosures

notes: Alumina is the largest single raw-material line in the smelter cost stack, so the direction of travel matters as much as the level. At roughly $328-330/t FOB Australia against a $3,179.00 3M official, alumina is about 10.3% of the metal price - historically low - and every public China indicator points lower still: SMM's 31-Jul analysis is headlined on the CNY 2,600/t threshold being under test as excess supply beats cost support, with the medium-term downtrend intact and national inventory continuing to build from the 7.028 Mt recorded at the last free weekly print.

THE PRECISE CURRENT INDEX LEVEL IS NOT PUBLISHED HERE because it sits behind SMM's paywall. What is public and sourced is the direction and the threshold under test. The last full free index print remains CNY 2,730.17/mt (16-Jul), carried in the table at that date rather than rolled forward.

The ex-China balance is loosening on restarts: EGA's Al Taweelah refinery is ramping after a three-and-a-half-month outage with full capability targeted at year-end and a debottlenecking expansion adding up to 50 kt, while S&P Global CERA models a 1.79 Mt global surplus for 2026 against 2.4 Mt in 2025. The offset arrives in Q4 - Rio Tinto's Yarwun will be cut 40% from October 2026 on tailings constraints, removing a tranche of Australian alumina from the surplus.

COMMERCIAL LOGIC OF A FALLING COST FLOOR: cheap alumina is the reason July's earnings season was uniformly strong across Alcoa, Hydro, Rio, South32 and Vedanta. It is also the reason the price floor is lower than it looks - a producer whose input costs are falling can defend a lower metal price without cutting output, which is precisely the configuration that turns a demand slowdown into a price slide rather than a supply response.

Structural exposure unchanged and public: roughly 9% of global primary aluminium capacity sits behind this waterway, more than 80% of Gulf metal is exported, and analysts covering the region pencil in 3-3.5 Mt of losses through 2026, near 5% of global primary supply.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: NO LONGER THE LESS BINDING CHOKEPOINT. Bab al Mandeb carried 31 commodity vessels on Friday 31-Jul, up from 29 a day earlier, but only after collapsing to a weekly low of 16 on 26-Jul following the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared on 20-Jul. The Houthis claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, prompting Saudi Arabia to divert crude exports to the Suez routing. With both Gulf chokepoints now impaired simultaneously, the freight and insurance wedge compounds on Gulf-origin metal and on Suez-routed alumina and semis alike - a materially worse configuration than the 'contested but flowing' reading carried through July.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk premiums for Gulf transits are quoted at 3-10% of hull value against roughly 0.25% before the conflict - a $250,000 premium becoming one exceeding $7 million per transit on a $100 million vessel (AL Circle / Reuters / The National reporting compiled 24-Jul). Cover quadrupled within three weeks of the first strikes and climbed toward 3% by early July before the current range. Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice, so the effective cost of a contested-strait transit rises before any cargo is damaged. Saturday's two attacks make near-term softening of these quotes improbable. This remains the single largest non-tariff cost wedge in Gulf-origin delivered prices.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: The Baltic Dry Index closed the month at 2,732 on Friday 31-Jul, up 59 points on the day and rebounding from 2,671, though still below the mid-July peak near 2,944 (Baltic Exchange via Hellenic Shipping News). No new print is published over the weekend. Dry-bulk direction matters most for bauxite and alumina freight into China, where Guinea shipped a record 114.8 Mt in H1. A firming BDI at the margin re-widens the freight leg of the alumina surplus math.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)
logistics.note: Drewry's World Container Index fell 4% to $4,374 per 40ft on 23-Jul (still the last published weekly print retrievable at this refresh), with Shanghai-Rotterdam at $4,824, after peaking at $4,639 on 09-Jul - the highest since September 2024 and roughly 61% above a year earlier. Direction is easing, but several carriers filed Emergency Fuel Surcharges effective August 2026 on continued Hormuz disruption, so realised container cost falls more slowly than the index and the August invoices now carry those surcharges.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: EGA's force majeure on European billet contracts, declared 12-Apr-2026, remained in force at the last public check (20-Jul). Contract mechanics - war-risk clauses, demurrage exposure and force-majeure triggers - remain live commercial variables wherever Gulf-origin metal or Hormuz-transiting alumina is involved, and Saturday's renewed attacks plus the Bab al Mandeb impairment widen the set of routes on which they bite. Two vessels switching off transponders in the strait on Friday is itself a contract-relevant fact: transponder-dark transits complicate cargo tracking, insurance verification and laytime evidence.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: Brent closed Friday 31-Jul at $87.93, up 1.21% on the session, and finished July roughly 24% higher on the month - the largest monthly advance since March and a Hormuz repricing at monthly scale rather than a spike (Trading Economics). Saturday's two vessel attacks near the strait land on top of that. The read-across is two-sided: energy is the largest single smelter cost line, so the same escalation that bids the metal raises the cost of making it, and European restart economics are the first casualty.

row.label: US Dollar Index
row.note: DXY 99.914 at the 31-Jul close, essentially flat on the session and holding below the 100 handle - the month-end configuration is a softening dollar into cooling US inflation. June core PCE printed +0.1% m/m (versus +0.2% expected) and 3.3% y/y (from 3.4%), with headline down to 3.7% from 4.1%. Cooler core inflation blunts the force of the FOMC's three-dissent hawkish minority and is dollar-negative at the margin, mechanically supportive for dollar-denominated metals. Still far above the 2% target, so 'tightening deferred, not removed' stands into the 15-16 September FOMC.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: EUR/USD 1.14850 on the 31-Jul LME FX fix (Westmetall MTLE), up from 1.14760 on 30-Jul; the ECB fixing matched and the BFIX reference printed 1.14860. The euro-area data cuts against the US direction: Eurostat's 31-Jul flash estimate put July inflation at 2.9% (from 2.8%) with core UP to 2.5% and ENERGY at 10.0% (from 8.5%) - the Middle East passthrough arriving in the CPI. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.25% on 23-Jul; an energy-driven reacceleration narrows its room to ease and keeps European smelter economics the marginal constraint, with TTF around EUR 59.07/MWh.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: Yuan 6.75254 at the 31-Jul close, marginally softer. THE DEMAND HEADLINE REMAINS THE PMI: July manufacturing 49.2 (June 50.3, consensus 50.1), the first sub-50 print since February 2026; non-manufacturing 49.0; composite 49.3. BUT THE PHYSICAL TAPE IS NOT CONFIRMING IT YET: SMM puts ingot inventory in major consumption regions at 953,000 t as at 30-Jul, through the 1 Mt mark, with 512,000 t (-35%) destocked from the early-May high and 53,000 t drawn in the week, and Foshan's premium widening 50 yuan/t to 115 yuan/t. row.label: USD/JPY
row.note: Yen 157.43 at the 31-Jul close, strengthening a further 1.31% and now well below 160, having been near 163.4 a week earlier. A firmer yen raises the local-currency cost of dollar-denominated metal for Japanese buyers - a real negative at the margin for MJP appetite with Q4-2026 CIF Japan negotiations expected to open around late August against an 11-year-high $395/t starting point.

row.label: US 10Y yield

catalysts.text: FIRST AUGUST LME OFFICIAL - now the single most informative number on the board. The cash-3M spread enters the month at +$17.00 after compressing $27.00 on Friday. Stabilising or rebuilding from here restores the physical-tightness read; sliding further toward flat, or into contango, confirms that late July's widening was a positioning squeeze that has now cleared. Watch it against the stock print, which drew again on the same session the spread halved

China Caixin manufacturing PMI for July - the private-survey cross-check on the official 49.2. Caixin skews toward smaller, export-oriented coastal manufacturers, so divergence between the two locates the weakness (state versus private sector) rather than confirming it economy-wide. It also arbitrates the tension between a contractionary survey and a physical tape that is still destocking

Whether LME stock breaks 260,000 t - the draw has run 23 consecutive published sessions at roughly -1,600 t/day, which brings the level into range within days. The more important variable is the AVAILABLE on-warrant component, at a 16-month low and dominated by Russian-origin material that many consumers will not take, so the deliverable buffer is thinner than the headline number

Hormuz and Bab al Mandeb transit counts - Hormuz ran about ten commodity vessels on Friday against more than 100 pre-war, with two further vessel attacks on Saturday 01-Aug; Bab al Mandeb recovered to 31 after a weekly low of 16 under the Houthi embargo on Saudi shipping. Two simultaneously impaired chokepoints is a materially different routing regime from July's, and it is the largest single swing factor in the premium structure into Q4 negotiations

SMM weekly China aluminium ingot and billet social inventory - the direct test of whether a contracting PMI translates into restocking. Inventory in major consumption regions has broken below 1 Mt to 953,000 t as at 30-Jul, cumulatively -512,000 t (-35%) from the early-May high, but SMM attributes the acceleration to supply contraction rather than demand, with weekly warehouse withdrawals pulling back to 127,700 t. China August PMIs and industrial output, then the 15-16 September FOMC with dots - whether July's 49.2 was a single-month distortion or the start of a demand downturn, and whether the Fed's three-dissent hawkish minority gains or loses ground. risks.text: THE PROMPT PREMIUM PROVED PARTLY SPECULATIVE - the cash-3M backwardation compressed from +$44.00 to +$17.00 in one session on the first official struck after China's 49.2 PMI, giving back 61% of a three-session widening run. A prompt premium that unwinds this fast on one demand print was not purely physical scarcity, and this risk moved from hypothetical to demonstrated in a single day. If Monday's official continues the slide toward flat, the tightness narrative loses its clearest public evidence

CHINA DEMAND HAS TURNED ON THE SURVEY DATA - July manufacturing PMI 49.2, the first contraction since February 2026, with non-manufacturing 49.0 and composite 49.3. The physical tape has NOT yet confirmed it (ingot inventory through 1 Mt at 953,000 t, Foshan premium +50 yuan to 115), but SMM attributes that destocking to supply contraction - liquid-aluminium share 78.3%, casting-ingot volume -15.1% y/y - rather than demand pull, with weekly warehouse withdrawals pulling back to 127,700 t. Monday's Caixin print is the cross-check

Indonesian, Chinese and now Western supply overwhelms the deficit - SMM reports outside-China daily-average output UP 1.6% month-on-month on Middle East and Iceland restarts, with Slovalco agreeing a 75 kt restart for Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals adding 75 kt/y at Marston by end-2026, Century's Mt. Holly back at full rate and Balco ramping. Indonesia adds ~705 kt in 2026 (+89% y/y) with Tsingshan planning 800 kt more at Weda Bay. The 2026 squeeze and the 2027-28 wave are the same trade in two acts

Falling alumina and raw materials remove cost-push support - SMM's 31-Jul analysis has the China alumina index testing the CNY 2,600/t threshold with excess supply beating cost support and the medium-term downtrend intact; bauxite ~$70/dmt on record Guinea shipments of 114.8 Mt in H1. A falling cost floor flatters margins today but lowers the level producers defend if demand keeps weakening, and it is now falling faster than a month ago

Tightening risk is DEFERRED, NOT REMOVED - the Fed held 9-3 and the Bank of England 6-3, each with three dissents FOR a hike; the cooler June core PCE (3.3%) leans against the hawks but the euro area's energy-led re-acceleration (July flash 2.9%, energy 10.0%) leans with them, and the US 10-year closed July at 4.74%. September's FOMC dot plot is the decision point for the dollar leg of the metals trade

Hormuz normalisation would erode the premium floor - but this risk RECEDED over the weekend. Two more vessels were attacked near the strait on Saturday 01-Aug, Friday's transit count was about ten commodity vessels against more than 100 pre-war, and Bab al Mandeb is now also impaired after the Houthi embargo on Saudi shipping. War-risk cover at 3-10% of hull value reprices on underwriters' cycles rather than transit counts, so even a genuine normalisation would unwind the insurance wedge slowly

Both positions are reported here as claims: Iran asserts closure, US Central Command asserts the waterway is open and reports rerouting 30 commercial vessels, disabling two and boarding two as at 31-Jul. CHINA'S DESTOCKING AND ITS PMI POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND THE ATTRIBUTION IS SMM'S, NOT AN INFERENCE DRAWN HERE. Inventory in major consumption regions fell to 953,000 t while the manufacturing PMI printed 49.2; SMM attributes the destocking to supply contraction (liquid-aluminium share 78.3%, casting-ingot volume -15.1% y/y) with weekly warehouse withdrawals pulling back to 127,700 t.
